newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks seen easing on loan repayment pressure.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks seen easing on loan repayment pressure.

text.p: Shares on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) are expected to fall amid selling pressure from investors under pressure to repay loans when the market reopens after a long weekend, brokers said.
"...Investors are under pressure to repay bank loans," said Golam Sarwar of Mahbub Morshed & Co.
Brokers say commercial banks have outstanding loans of more than 500 million taka with investors who have taken advances against their shares.
The banks are asking the defaulted investors, who failed to repay loans before the end of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June), to clear their dues immediately.

Sarwar said investors were also seeking funds for IPOs (initial public offering) which are due in coming weeks. Shamarita Hospital Ltd, Uttara Finance Investment Ltd. Gem Knittwear Fabrics Ltd and C&C Kamal Textile Mills Ltd were offering IPOs worth about 250 million taka in July and August. ($ 1 = 43.65 taka)
The DSE index dropped 13.2 points or 1.18 percent to 1,098.35 on Wednesday.
The market was closed on Thursday for an opposition strike, ahead of the normal Friday and Saturday weekend.
